chunks: My scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Sarah al-Madaini, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj or someone else named al-Husayn, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on one of three nights, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sin and what followed. I said, Which of the nights, may I be sacrificed for you? He said: The night of al-Fitr, the night of al-Adha, and the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban.

key_terms.زَارَ: visited (specifically for ziyarah/pilgrimage to a shrine)
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ النِّصْفِ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ: the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What are the three nights when visiting Imam Husayn's grave leads to complete forgiveness of sins?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* emphasizes the immense spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s shrine on three pivotal nights: Laylat al-Fitr, Laylat al-Adha, and Laylat al-Nisf min Sha'ban. In Shia tradition, these nights are viewed as times of divine mercy and forgiveness, where the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt amplifies the reward for pilgrims, granting them absolution for both past and future sins.
